sections.title: Names and distinct present communities
sections.text: Lenape is broader than any one government. Delaware Nation’s history distinguishes its Anadarko community from Delaware Tribe of Indians and other Lenape governments. Similar names do not make these institutions interchangeable.

sections.title: An eastern homeland and overlapping reading labels
sections.text: The Tribe’s introduction locates Lenape history in the Delaware Valley. This people-level route overlaps the preserved Delaware (Lenape) entry; both labels remain available. Individual governments and language communities need their own specifically supported identities.

sections.title: Reading the Walking Purchase critically
sections.text: Jennings examines the 1737 Walking Purchase through land papers and competing testimony. He argues that proprietary manipulation affected both dispossession and the records used to describe it. Read this as an attributed historical argument: the original manuscripts have not been independently checked here.

sections.title: What the 1778 treaty actually says
sections.text: The Fort Pitt treaty addresses peace, military passage, trade and territorial guarantees. Article VI proposes a state headed by the Delaware nation with congressional representation, expressly subject to congressional approval. A proposed arrangement is not proof that a state or seat was created. The document’s terms also do not demonstrate their fulfillment.

sections.title: A specifically scoped Texas connection
sections.text: Delaware Nation connects its Absentee Delaware history with movement toward Texas and the Brazos reservation. Lipscomb’s Texas reference adds diplomacy, scouting and reserve-removal context. These accounts describe particular groups and stages; they do not place every Lenape community in Texas or establish all present families’ descent. Detailed migration and relocation chronology remains unfinished.

sections.title: An Ontario community’s own account
sections.text: Eelünaapéewi Lahkéewiit’s Our Story follows a Moravian-connected community through displacement and rebuilding at Fairfield and New Fairfield. This is an Ontario community’s retrospective, distinct from the Oklahoma government also called Delaware Nation. Its wider historical claims and battle interpretation require comparison rather than automatic adoption.

sections.title: Learning through the Talking Dictionary
sections.text: The Lenape Talking Dictionary identifies its main language scope as Southern Unami. Its introductory lesson explains spelling and everyday greetings, while documentation identifies speakers and other contributors. Selected entry text was read; audio playback was not tested. This resource does not stand for every Lenape language variety, and recordings retain their individual provenance.

sections.title: Language programs in a dated account
sections.text: Writing in 2002, Rementer and Pearson describe several generations of Oklahoma language classes, learning materials and the early dictionary project. Their different community relationships are explicit. The paper is useful program history, not a current speaker census or proof of learning outcomes. Language loss must not be read as disappearance of a people.

sections.title: Reading path and remaining work
sections.text: Start with community accounts, compare the treaty’s actual terms, and use the language resources within their stated scope. Jennings provides a focused example of archival criticism. This is a reviewed first reading foundation. Texas primary records, broader community perspectives and later histories still need substantial work; no completion or community endorsement is claimed.

overview: Lenape histories connect an eastern homeland with distinct present communities and different displacement routes. This reading foundation includes community accounts, a primary treaty, language education and critical scholarship. Its Texas coverage is introductory and specifically scoped.
relationshipNote: The original Delaware (Lenape) entry and this entry substantially overlap; keep both search labels while connecting them. Lenape people-level history, specific current governments and language varieties are not interchangeable. Preserve Munsee and community-specific routes without inferred identity or descent.

initialAdequacy.rationale: Six actual-content works provide a varied first reading foundation, with two supporting/index cards excluded. Quantity does not resolve uneven regional coverage, source disagreements, incomplete Texas primary evidence, language breadth or later histories. No automatic adequacy, completion or community review is claimed.
